thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: latency_slo_alert (p99) for service=continuous-batcher in prod-us-east — triggered 2m ago. Pager: @alex @maria

alex: I'm on it. Seeing p99 spike on cbatcher-shard-7 around 10:02 UTC. Dashboard shows streaming tail jumps and backlog rising.

maria: reported by synthetic checks?

incident-bot: Alert details: metric=latency_p99, value=3.2s, SLO=1.2s, affected_routes=chat_streaming/*, recent_increase=5x over baseline. Linked: https://grafana.redwood/graphs/CB-201

sam: I'm pulling host metrics. KV cache evictions up and GPU utilization slightly below max. Could be scheduling fairness causing large batches to stall streaming lanes.

jin: Any recent rollout? model-driver or scheduler changes?

alex: No model rollouts in last 24h. We did push a scheduler tweak last week that increased max_concurrent_batches to 6.

maria: timeline: spike starts ~10:01, p95 rises to ~800ms, p99 to 3.2s. Streaming sessions show stalls (clients hang mid-stream).

sam: grabbing heap and scheduler traces. Suspicious logs: "batch_wait_timeout=1200ms, batch_dispatch_delay=2400ms" for many streaming requests.

alex: That smells like mixed-seqlen packing creating a giant batch waiting for long tokens to finish. Continuous-batcher tries to fill batch up to max_size before dispatch.

jin: Quick mitigation idea: reduce cont_batch_max_size and enable seqlen-aware-early-flush. Can we toggle via runtime flags?

maria: Yes, runtime knob path: /config/continuous_batcher -> {max_size, early_flush_pct}. We can lower max_size from 1024 to 256 and set early_flush_pct to 0.4.

sam: Also we should throttle long-seq requests by lowering stream_concurrency per connection. That avoids long tails hogging the scheduler.

alex: I will patch config on prod-us-east canary first. Pushing change now to shard-7 only. Command: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/configs/continuous_batcher/shard-7 -d '{"max_size":256,"early_flush_pct":0.4}'`

ops: deploybot: Received config update request for shard-7. Initiating rolling apply.

incident-bot: Change applied to shard-7 (10:12:45 UTC). Monitoring for 2m.

maria: After change p95 -> 320ms, p99 -> 1.1s on shard-7. Streaming stalls count dropped by ~85%. Good sign.

sam: Let's apply to other affected shards incrementally (shard-6, shard-8) with 1-minute observation windows.

jin: Before expanding, also flip on seqlen-aware-packing in canary: `early_flush_by_length=true` to avoid waiting for outlier long sequences.

alex: Applied to shard-6 and 8. Commands: `opsctl config apply --shards 6,8 --max-size 256 --early-flush 0.4 --early-flush-by-length true`

ops: deploybot: Rolling apply started for shards 6 and 8.

maria: Telemetry across region: p99 back to ~1.0s region-wide after shards updated. But dedicated-customer X still sees intermittent 2s spikes.

sam: Looking at logs for that customer's requests — they send long multi-turn prompts with repeated embeddings in a single stream. Sequence length distribution is skewed (tail > 12k tokens). Our per-client packing threshold needs to cap sequences per batch.

alex: For immediate mitigation, enable per-customer stream_rate_limit and cap their max_seq_per_batch to 4. I'll add a targeted rule for customer X.

incident-bot: Rule change applied for customer X: stream_rate_limit=2rps, max_seq_per_batch=4.

maria: Confirmed customer X p99 dropped to 1.1s post-targeted rule. Customer success pinged — CS: "we saw reduced lag, please follow up with root cause".

jin: Root cause hypothesis: the continuous batcher combined mixed-sequence requests and waited to fill batches up to a very large size (1024) after scheduler tweak, giving priority to batch fullness over streaming latency. Fairness policy favored throughput at expense of tail latency for streaming.

sam: Evidence: scheduler traces show long queue-time for streaming class, and GPU kernel time doesn't spike — waits are in queue. KV cache evictions increased due to large batch windows and concurrent prefetches.

alex: Next steps: 1) Keep reduced max_size and early-flush-by-length enabled for 24h. 2) Roll a scheduler policy change: add queue-priority for streaming lanes and token-bucket to limit batch wait per-request. 3) Create a post-incident test harness with mixed sequence-length synthetic traffic to prevent regressions. 4) Follow up with a customer impact report.

maria: I'll own the customer impact blurb and notify CS + support with timestamps and mitigation steps.

jin: I'll open an RFC for scheduler fairness change with perf numbers and risk assessment.

sam: I'll script the synthetic load test and run in staging tomorrow.

alex: Handoff to @maria for next 4 hours. I'll be on backup. If anything regresses, page escalation list.

maria: Taking handoff. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved for now — monitoring continues. Incident severity: high (customer impact limited to specific tenants), mitigations applied.

alex: closing thread, will follow up with a short postmortem including timeline, config diffs, and Grafana panels.

maria: adding notes to incident tracker: https://tracker.redwood/incidents/CB-2211

sam: leaving a runbook note: prefer `max_size<=512` and `early_flush_by_length=true` for streaming-heavy clusters.

jin: 👍
